It will actually display at about 155 x 62 pixels, and even 95 x 38 pixels on small phones. Design for strong THUMBNAIL LEGIBILITY rather than a detailed poster.

Campaign: Mina Misteriosa (mysterious mine), maximum prize R$ 8.888, 24 chances per day. The user wants VERY FEW WORDS, clearly readable. No website URL or brand logo.
Render ONLY these exact three text groups:
"MINA MISTERIOSA"
"ATÉ R$ 8.888"
"24x/DIA"
The qualifier ATÉ means the prize is up to that amount and must remain visible. 24x/DIA means 24 chances each day. Keep the acute accent in ATÉ, all four eights with a period after the first: 8.888. No other words or numbers.

Composition:
The text dominates the LEFT 73–76% of the tile; the RIGHT 24–27% shows a cropped elephant-headed fantasy treasure guardian's friendly, dignified face and gold headdress, matching the campaign's elephant theme. It must be secondary and must not steal room from the lettering. Only the head, shoulders and perhaps a small part of one treasure vessel; no tiny full-body character.
Three bold, simple visual beats, all aligned and optically balanced:
1. "MINA MISTERIOSA" in ONE large clean headline line near the top, very bold slightly condensed italic SANS-SERIF silver-white capitals with a modest warm metallic edge and dark outline. NOT serif, NOT thin decorative type. Use most of the text area width.
2. "ATÉ R$ 8.888" in the middle as the largest, strongest line. The four gold eights are the dominant focal point, chunky and broad, with controlled 3D bevel and clear deep-charcoal outline. ATÉ and R$ can be a little smaller, but never tiny. No excessive extrusion, no unreadable currency.
3. "24x/DIA" in a single compact, clearly legible pill near lower left/center below the amount, bright warm ivory letters on a quiet dark copper inset. Make this large enough to read at thumbnail scale. No long supporting sentence or fine print.
Keep at least 5% safety on every side. No overlapping critical text. Avoid big unused margins. Amount first, name second, cadence third, character fourth.

NEW COLOR PALETTE: warm CHARCOAL and AMBER / BURNISHED COPPER. Deep charcoal #191719, warm espresso #38251b, subtle bronze #70482c, amber light #d99b4a, champagne gold #ffe2a1 and pearl-white #fff7eb. Do not use the previous banners' purple, blue, burgundy or green backgrounds. Tiny amethyst details on jewelry may connect to the site's purple brand.
Background: a cinematic softly defocused mysterious mine / treasure chamber, shown through just two or three broad warm stone facets and one amber side glow. Moderate depth but VERY LITTLE fine detail because this is tiny. Keep the area behind all typography nearly uniform dark charcoal-brown. No dense architecture, no piles of coins, no confetti, no banners, no balloons. One or two coarse gem shapes at the right base are enough.
Guardian: refined premium 3D elephant-headed treasure guardian with warm copper-gray skin, a gold jeweled headpiece and rich dark copper clothing, tasteful and dignified, softly lit with amber rim light. Large clear ears and curved trunk form an instantly recognizable silhouette. No logo, no rabbit mascot.
Style: cinematic lighting and commercially polished 3D material finish, but big simple shapes, crisp high-contrast typography and a controlled number of details. NO ornate frames, NO gold plaque full of small type, NO extra slogans, NO br893.com, NO URL, NO watermark, NO buttons, NO other amounts, NO pale unreadable words. Full-bleed horizontal artwork, no white border or mockup.
